speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. Agent; you mentioned experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath. To begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do they worsen at any specific time of day or with certain activities?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned symptoms started a month ago and worsened with activity and at night, but you also had fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago. Are you currently taking any medications, particularly for allergies or asthma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiolitis Obliterans secondary to a recent viral infection.

The history of an upper respiratory infection 8 weeks ago followed by progressive exertional dyspnea and nocturnal cough is highly suggestive of post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans. To confirm this, I need to see a Chest_X-Ray and request a CT scan of the chest. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT
